doc: SYSTEM-SPEC-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25: "something's missing in the core ultra-stable template that's not saying, hey, this is what an ultra-stable system is. This is how ultra-stable runs. This is how ultra-stable bootstraps. This is how ultra-stable becomes autonomous and achieves criticality."). The definition of an Ultrastable system, as data. scripts/system.py renders SYSTEM.md from it and from the code of record (bootstrap stages from bootstrap/bootstrap.py, tick steps from worker/src/tick.js, ignition stages from worker/src/ignition.js, the criticality formula from autonomy/criticality.json, standing rules from agents/AGENTS.md), and `scripts/system.py --check` fails when SYSTEM.md is stale, a clause's probe fails in this kit, or a standing rule has no enforcement here that is not on the shrink-only not_in_kit list. Every probe is a path inside this kit: grep:<path>::<regex> or file:<path>.

clauses.text: An Ultrastable system is an organization of virtual managers and staff that runs itself on a server-side clock and closes its own loops. A person writes one file, IDEA.md; everything after that is the system's work.

It is for something that has to keep running. An idea qualifies only when all four hold: a loop it must close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep and improvement that never end, and a running cost the owner accepts. The bootstrapper refuses anything else before it hires a role or provisions anything.

Autonomous means the system has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Every loop has a trigger, an owner, a closing probe and a write-back, and every open item has an owner, a trigger and a probe.

The owner supplies direction, the idea and a budget. The system does the back end: errors, credentials, deploys, retries and repairs, recorded where the owner can audit them and never handed to the owner to act on.

Everything runs server-side: a Cloudflare Worker with its own D1 database and cron, and GitHub Actions on its built-in token. Nothing depends on a person's computer, a desktop app or an open chat session.
If it is not in code, it does not exist. The repository and the database are the only memory; chat, tool memory and documents nothing reads are not storage.
probe: grep:agents/AGENTS.md::If it is not in code, it does not exist

clauses.text: The heartbeat is one tick every 10 minutes from the Worker's cron. A second producer, POST /pulse/watch, runs a tick when the newest one is older than two intervals, so one silent trigger never stops the clock.

A tick runs every step listed below, and the same cron runs the loops listed after them. A failing step is recorded and filed as work, and the other steps still run. Each tick writes its report to tick_runs and /health.
Work is items with a claim, a prediction logged before the change and a closing probe after it. An item leaves the active set only with a disposition; reconcile reopens any that left without one.

The only pause is the interrupt gate: a step that is irreversible and identity-bound with no reversible path. It becomes one gate card with a default in effect and a closing probe; the system works on in the meantime.
One halt stops every recurring path: the Worker variable HALT=1 stops the cron, the watch route and the webhooks. Pages keep serving.
Every model call is paid from the owner's monthly budget through one governor; the budget is a number in the repository, never a promise.
bootstrap/bootstrap.py runs the stages below in order. It is idempotent: running it again changes nothing that is already true.
A stage that cannot finish is recorded as blocked with its reason and becomes a backlog item with a closing probe; the boot continues with the next stage. A missing credential never stops the boot.
The boot is accepted only when the system's own drills show at least a year unattended (year_gate) and its /health answers live (verify_live).

From its first deploy every system serves all of its public surfaces together: a web page with the Built on Ultrastable footer, /health, the discovery manifest, the knowledge graph's read side, and a listing in the ultrastable.io directory. No gate may hide one of them.
A system needs no key from its owner when it is hosted: the platform deploys it through its own OIDC route and gives it its repository from the seed.

sections.title: How it becomes autonomous and reaches criticality

clauses.text: The system reads its own stage every tick from evidence it recorded itself; nothing is declared. A stage is reached when the reading holds for it and every stage below, and lost when it stops holding. The first unmet stage is filed as IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it, and only the same reading closes it.
Bootstrapped means instrumented or above: the system stands, runs and measures itself. Critical and self-sustaining are the two stages above that.

Criticality is a number. k_eff = (credited verified deploys + credited loop-originated items) / (spend units + human touches) over the window. The system is critical when k_eff stays at or above k_min, and self-sustaining when it stays critical with no open ignition gaps and no human touches.
Self-reference is the multiplier: k_self counts only deploys the system originated and shipped on itself. A deploy an outside session drove raises k_eff, never k_self.
The standing goal is a year unattended: a simulated 10th-percentile horizon of at least 365 days, with every fault class it names drilled against the real recovery code.

Trust is computed per surface and action class from recorded outcomes, and widens scope only through a reviewed change to autonomy/policy.json. Trust never reaches the interrupt gate, secrets or harness permissions.

not_in_kit_doc: Rule ids whose enforcement lives only in the platform repository (foundation/, site/, deploy/, doctrine/ outside this kit). A seeded system inherits the rule as an instruction; the platform checks it for every system it hosts. Shrink-only: a new rule must ship its check into the kit or the check fails.
kit_enforcement_doc: A rule whose bullet cites platform paths but whose behaviour this kit carries under its own names: each probe must pass here, so the map cannot claim code that is not in the kit.
